_meta.asset_kind: type-genus declension-stem lexicon for higher-rank name derivation
_meta.status: M0 draft. Names of suprageneric taxa are formed from the GENITIVE (declension) STEM of the type-genus name, never from the nominative. Only entries individually flagged verified:true may be used to assert compliance; every emitted name additionally has to appear in 'attested_higher_rank_names' with verified:true, otherwise the engine returns needs_review / compliant=None.
provenance: ICNP (2022), rules on names of suprageneric taxa: family and order names are formed from the stem of the name of the type genus plus the termination -aceae / -ales (exact article numbers are NOT re-verified here — see rule_citation_status).

SeqCode curation guide (local snapshot seqcode-documentation/guide/curation.md:158-165): 'Confirm that the correct rank ... families should end in the suffix -aceae, orders ... -ales, classes ... -ia, phyla ... -ota.' and step 2: 'Check that the name is formed from the inferred stem of the type genus name.'
LPSN (lpsn.dsmz.de) published family/order/class/phylum names, cited per entry as the anchor that attests the stem.
_meta.rule_citation_status: verified: false — the ICNP article/rule numbers behind -aceae/-ales/-ota/-ia were not checked against the code text in this repository. The suffix FORMS are cross-checked against LPSN usage (the LPSN status label vocabulary; the stem-derivation requirement is cross-checked against the SeqCode curation guide quoted above.
_meta.how_to_extend: Add the genus to 'genera' with the stem that the PUBLISHED higher-rank name actually uses (that is the only machine-checkable evidence), the anchor name and its source. Never add a stem inferred from memory: leave the genus out so the documented 'fallback_rules' apply, which are flagged needs_review by design.
_meta.composition_note: suffix composition (engine/generate.py::_compose_higher_rank): stem + suffix, with Latin vowel coalescence: a stem ending in -i followed by a suffix beginning with i loses the suffix's i (clostridi + ia -> Clostridia, corynebacteri + ineae -> Corynebacterineae, acidimicrobi + idae -> Acidimicrobidae). Attested by those three published names.

Bacillus.source: LPSN: Bacillaceae, Bacillales, Bacillota; class Bacilli (protected name)

Deinococcus.source: LPSN: family Deinococcaceae, order Deinococcales, phylum Deinococcota

Treponema.source: LPSN: Treponemataceae (irregular: -ma stem is -mat, NOT the nominative minus -a)

Crenarchaeum.source: LPSN: Crenarchaeota (phylum), Crenarchaeales; family name derived stem keeps the Greek -o-

Acidimicrobium.source: LPSN: Acidimicrobiaceae, subclass Acidimicrobidae, class Acidimicrobiia

Bdellovibacter.source: LPSN: Bdellovibrionaceae — counter-example proving a mechanical '-er -> identity' rule is unsafe, hence the lexicon

Klebsiella.source: LPSN: Klebsiellaceae (note: the family is NOT Enterobacteriaceae in current LPSN usage)

Escherichia.source: LPSN: family of Escherichia is Enterobacteriaceae/Morganellaceae per current taxonomy — stem entry only, the TYPE GENUS of the family is a different genus (typification is not machine-checkable)

fallback_rules.note: Greek neuters in -ma have the genitive stem in -mat; dropping only -a (-> Treponemaceae) is a known error.

fallback_rules.anchor: Clostridium -> clostridi (Clostridiaceae), Mycobacterium -> mycobacteri (Mycobacteriaceae), Crenarchaeum -> crenarchae (Crenarchaeota)

class.source: ICNP protected/conserved class name; listed in rules.json conserved_names; SeqCode curation guide treats -ia as the recommendation, Bacilli as the historical exception
class.note: The mechanical form 'Bacillia' is NOT a published name and must never be emitted (scripts/verify_examples.py 'NOT Bacillia').

subtribe.name: Streptomycinae
subtribe.source: rules.json rank_suffix_examples (M0 anchored list) — NOT re-verified against LPSN inside this repository
subtribe.note: Tribal ranks are built on the 'Streptomyco-' stem (tribe Streptomyceae, subtribe Streptomycinae), NOT on the family stem 'Streptomycet-' (Streptomycetaceae). Mechanical composition would give 'Streptomycetinae', so this exception exists precisely because the regular rule cannot reproduce the anchored example (a machine check catches exactly this).
